correctness.rationale: For girth at least six, no distance-two pair has two midpoints and any centered neighborhood simplex collapses relative to the original graph by the explicit decreasing-cardinality matching. A noncentered clique triangle must be one alternating triple of a simple six-cycle; if it had a fourth compatible vertex, another six-cycle would share at least one graph edge, contradicting the all-six-cycle edge-disjointness hypothesis. Therefore exactly two noncentered maximal triangles occur per hexagon and no higher noncentered simplices. They attach twice along the same primitive six-edge cycle of G; attach/collapse the first disk against a different private edge per hexagon, then attach the second disk to create an S2. Remaining cycle rank is b-h, integral kernel generated by disjoint primitive six-cycles and H2 by corresponding sphere pairs. Independently reconstructed shortest-path Rips faces and boundary ranks for C6, theta(3,3,4), theta(3,3,5), and the excluded theta(3,3,3); noncentered face counts were 2,2,2,8 respectively, and the excluded case has two noncentered tetrahedra. Finite examples corroborate, not prove, the all-graph argument.
correctness.risk: The homotopy claim uses graph-vertex shortest-path distances and inclusive threshold 2; applying it to metric-graph edge interior points or overlapping hexagons is invalid.

final_claim: For finite connected simple graphs of girth at least six whose distinct simple six-cycles have pairwise disjoint edge sets and with at least one hexagon, the inclusive scale-two graph-vertex Vietoris–Rips complex is homotopy equivalent to \( igvee^{b(G)-h(G)}S^1ee igvee^{h(G)}S^2\), and the map from the original graph has primitive integral first-homology kernel spanned by all six-cycle classes and independent H2 generators per six-cycle.
limitations: Girth≥6 and pairwise edge-disjointness apply to ALL simple six-cycles.
Only shortest-path metric on graph vertices and inclusive scales 1 and 2.
Does not claim an equivariant collapse or higher-scale topology.
